html:
SMTO-CMP-0003 — SMTO couldn't accept how the AI said the task was finished

GUID: 26b65c64-44cd-428d-b7fa-0e85ddfe1fdc
Slug: invalid-direct-completion
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI model sent its "I'm done" signal in the wrong format, so SMTO didn't accept it. The rejected signal didn't run anything, and work already finished and its results are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the task's steps and latest reply to see what SMTO already finished. Those results are saved. Do not rerun those steps. This error is only about the AI's finish signal, so the finished work itself is still valid.
  2. If the task shows Partial · resumable, select Resume on the task. SMTO asks the AI to resend a correct finish signal using results it already has, without repeating any step.
  3. Don't select Restart task for this problem. Restart begins a fresh attempt and doesn't undo earlier actions, so changes could happen twice.
  4. If this keeps happening, ask the person who manages SMTO to choose a more capable Main model in Settings › Setup › Model routing. The finish signal is written by the AI model, and some models follow SMTO's format less reliably.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and SMTO's final reply appears under it.

If it still fails

  • Open Technical details, select Copy error details, and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with the model the task used. Don't restart the task to fix this; the finished work is already saved.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server rejected the model's runtime completion metadata (__smto_completion or __smto_terminal_output) because it was malformed, unavailable for that decision or in conflict with the frozen output contract, or repeated rejections reached the completion-correction bound.

What this means

  • Runtime completion metadata is malformed, unavailable for the selected result, conflicts with the frozen output declaration or appears in competing proposals; bounded protocol recovery can also stop here. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Runtime completion metadata is malformed, unavailable for the selected result, conflicts with the frozen output declaration or appears in competing proposals; bounded protocol recovery can also stop here.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact metadata/protocol reason and retained attempt, independently of operation success.

How to fix it

  • Read the rejection reason (invalid_enum, invalid_type, invalid_object_shape, unavailable, inappropriate_capability, missing/invalid/frozen_output_contract or completion_protocol_failed) in the run's completion.rejected and guard.strike events. Resume the run so the model re-declares completion against the existing receipts; Do not rerun successful operations merely to repair the metadata. If one model keeps failing this protocol, switch the Main model under Settings › Setup › Model routing or review the schema.strict_validation and protocol.completion_retry_bound Agent Checks.
  • Preserve the retained answer and receipts. Correct the completion declaration against existing evidence or continue only unfinished work. Do not rerun successful operations merely to repair completion metadata.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use retained evidence to correct completion metadata; replay of completed operations is not required to repair the declaration.

How to verify the fix

  • A corrected declaration matches current evidence and the accepted output contract without replay.

What not to do

  • Do not restart completed work merely because completion metadata was rejected.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
